title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཙ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 96)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio of a Madhyamaka commentary on Mulamadhyamakakarika ch. 7 (refutation of abiding, sthiti), shelved in the dbu ma section where it belongs.

ocr_errors.problem: final ས of སྐྱེས dropped; '#' uncertainty markers left in the text

ocr_errors.image: negation reads as མ/མི at this resolution; the argument requires མ་གནས་པ 'not (yet) abiding'
ocr_errors.problem: negation particle doubtful, flagged by the engine; both translations take the required sense

ocr_errors.image: sense requires གནས་པ་གནས་པས་རང་གི…; the word is not cleanly legible in c2/c3
ocr_errors.problem: probable dropped instrumental 'by abiding'; both translations restore it

tr_errors_A.problem: page-initial fragment (the head noun, likely 'destruction-ness' given the next sentence, is on the previous leaf) rendered as an opaque phrase

tr_errors_A.english: At that time, in dependence upon what could one claim endurance exists?
tr_errors_A.problem: relative clause 'those in reference to which abiding is asserted' recast as a separate question; argument intact

tr_errors_A.english: If it is produced after having arisen,
tr_errors_A.problem: 'if the already-born produces' made passive; recoverable from the next line

tr_errors_A.english: cause anything, let alone itself, to endure?

tr_errors_B.problem: page-initial fragment filled with a doctrinally loaded guess ('no selfhood', i.e. absence of self-nature); the context (next sentence: destruction as the mark of a thing, 'if that is absent') points to the absence of destruction, so a reader is told a claim the page does not make

tr_errors_B.english: when we speak of abiding in relation to anything

has not yet stayed / already stayed … abiding

pages.prefer_reason: Neither version has a serious error and both render every sentence and verse on the image; A is marginally better because B fills the page-initial fragment with an unsupported doctrinal claim ('no selfhood') where A stays neutral, a moderate-vs-minor difference only.

adjudication.claim: ཅི་སྟེ་སྐྱེས་པས་སྐྱེད་བྱེད་ན passivised as 'produced after having arisen'
adjudication.why: Image reads སྐྱེས་པས་སྐྱེད་བྱེད་ན (agentive, active); A's passive is a minor slip, sense recoverable.
Same reading on the image; minor in both.
Image line 1 begins ཉིད་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ with no head noun; 'selfhood' is supplied, and the next sentence about destruction points elsewhere; I rate it moderate, not minor.

adjudication.claim: A renders terminology more precisely and reads more naturally (prefer A)
adjudication.why: Stylistic preference is not a ground; both are faithful line by line against the image. My preference for A rests on B's supplied 'selfhood' claim instead.
Image shows སྐྱེས where OCR has སྐྱེ#, and '#' markers remain in the text; minor slips only, score 4.

book_verdict: A clean Derge folio with near-complete OCR and two faithful English versions of the MMK ch. 7 commentary on abiding; nothing an expert would flag on sight beyond stray '#' uncertainty markers.
